name: Generic 4K Dash Cam
whySpecs: 4K dash cams write about 50 to 100 Mbps depending on the model and codec. V30 guarantees 30 MB/s sustained, above that rate. Loop recording rewrites the whole card over and over, so high-endurance cards, which manufacturers rate in recording hours, outlast standard cards.

faq.q: What's the difference between dash cam and regular microSD cards?
faq.a: Endurance. High-endurance cards are rated for tens of thousands of hours of continuous recording; SanDisk rates its MAX Endurance line at up to 120,000 hours. Standard cards carry no such rating.

faq.q: Can I use a regular fast microSD card in a dash cam?
faq.a: It works, but wears out sooner. Speed doesn't help with constant rewrites. A high-endurance card is the better buy.

faq.q: Is 64GB or 128GB better for a dash cam?
faq.a: 128GB for most drivers. At 4K, 64GB holds roughly 1.5 to 3 hours and 128GB about double. For parking mode, buy 256GB.

notes: Universal dash cam recommendation. Works with Rexing, Viofo, Garmin, VANTRUE, and most aftermarket 4K cameras.

name: Viofo A229 Pro Dual Dash Cam
whySpecs: The A229 Pro is a 4K front plus 2K rear (or interior) dash cam that saves each channel's files to separate folders on a single microSD card. Viofo supports cards up to 512GB and recommends high-endurance U3 cards.

faq.q: Do I need two cards for the Viofo A229 Pro?
faq.a: No. The A229 Pro has one microSD slot and records front, rear and interior footage to the same card.

faq.q: What size card should I get for the A229 Pro?
faq.a: 256GB for most drivers, 512GB for long parking-mode sessions. Two or three channels share one card, so it fills faster than a single-channel camera.

faq.q: Can I use a regular microSD card in the A229 Pro?
faq.a: It will record, but loop recording wears it out. Use a high-endurance U3 card.

notes: Professional dual-channel dash cam. Requires dual High Endurance cards for reliable operation.

name: Viofo T130 Pro
searchTerms: best sd card for viofo t130 pro
whySpecs: Viofo specifically restricts the T130 Pro to UHS-I U3-rated, dashcam/high-endurance microSD cards, not general-purpose consumer cards. The camera loop-records continuously, overwriting old footage in a cycle that wears out standard cards within weeks in a hot windshield environment. Viofo caps supported capacity at 256GB, with 128GB called out as the preferable, more reliable size.

faq.q: Can I use a regular fast microSD card in the T130 Pro?
faq.a: No. Viofo's own guidance restricts the T130 Pro to U3-rated, dashcam/high-endurance cards. Standard consumer cards aren't built for continuous loop-overwrite recording and tend to fail within weeks of dash cam use, especially in hot windshield-mounted conditions.

faq.q: What's the maximum card size for the T130 Pro?
faq.a: 256GB is the maximum supported capacity, with 128GB called out as preferable for reliability. Bigger isn't automatically better here. Viofo's guidance favors a properly rated endurance card over maxing out capacity.

faq.q: Why do dash cam cards need to be 'high-endurance'?
faq.a: The T130 Pro continuously overwrites old footage in a loop, which wears out standard consumer microSD cards far faster than normal photo/video use. High-endurance cards are built with this write/erase cycle pattern in mind and last years instead of weeks.

notes: Restrict affiliate output strictly to High-Endurance/U3 cards rated for continuous overwrite loops. Explicitly warn against standard consumer cards — heat + loop-recording wear kills them early in hot windshields. Per Viofo's own guidance, max 256GB, 128GB preferable.

name: BlackVue DR970X
whySpecs: Continuous parking and driving recording needs a card that can handle sustained overwrite cycles. Cards over 64GB ship formatted as exFAT, which BlackVue doesn't support, so they must be reformatted to FAT32 in the BlackVue app before use.

faq.q: Why do I need to reformat my card for the BlackVue DR970X?
faq.a: Cards larger than 64GB ship pre-formatted as exFAT, which BlackVue's firmware doesn't support. Use the BlackVue app to reformat the card to FAT32 before installing it, or the camera won't record properly.

notes: Base DR970X caps at 256GB; only the DR970X Plus / DR970X Plus LTE Series II support up to 1TB. Official spec only requires Class 10/U1 — U3 is BlackVue's recommendation, not a hard requirement.

name: Thinkware U3000
whySpecs: Continuous front/rear recording needs a card rated for sustained writes. Thinkware's own compatibility documentation caps the standard U3000 at 256GB. A separate U3000 Pro variant supports more, so don't confuse the two when shopping.

faq.q: What's the maximum SD card size for the Thinkware U3000?
faq.a: 256GB is the max for the standard U3000, per Thinkware's own compatibility documentation. The separate U3000 Pro variant supports larger cards, so don't assume the two share the same ceiling when shopping.

notes: Dropped the 'rejects cards without continuous write stability' claim from the original brief — no official Thinkware source backs it; this looks like SEO embellishment of a generic 'use quality cards' recommendation.
